A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ia(+) cells are increased in absolute numbers in some patients with primary immunodeficiency, but are not the major T cell subpopulation responsible for immunoglobulin synthesis in these patients.
Ia(+) cells are increased in number in some immune deficiency patients but that their functional role in the regulation of immunoglobulin synthesis remains uncertain.
the Ia(+) cells in immune deficiency may not be the same as those present in normal individuals and that the function of the Ia(++) T cells may be different in immune deficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no uniform abnormality in proportions of T gamma, T mu, or Ia(+)T cells among a large group of adult immune deficiency patients.
